Aren't you going to the garden club's open house on Saturday? (A) Yes, I'm really looking forward to it. (B) They're selling plants and garden tools there. (C) In the back courtyard, near the fountain.

M1: Hi, I'm putting together a cheese board for a dinner party this weekend, and I could really use some help choosing. W1: Of course, I'd be happy to help. How many guests will you be serving? M1: There'll be eight of us at the table. W1: In that case, I'd suggest our aged cheddar. It's rich and full of flavor, and it pairs well with almost anything. M1: That does sound nice, though I'm not sure it's quite right for the whole group. W1: No problem at all. Why don't I cut you a small piece to try before you decide? M1: Great idea. I'll taste it right now, and then I'll figure out what else to add.

M1: Good morning, and welcome to Harborview Restaurant Supply. Is there something I can help you track down today? W1: Yes, thanks. I manage a café a couple of blocks over, and we're reopening this weekend after some renovations. I need a large order of dinner plates and coffee mugs — several dozen of each — and I'm really hoping they can reach me before Friday. M1: That's a sizable order, so let me pull up our warehouse records and make sure we're holding that many here, not over at our supplier's depot. If they're on hand, I could load them into my own van and drop them by your café this afternoon. The one catch is, for a bulk purchase this size, I'll have to get my manager's approval before I can finalize it.

W1: Good afternoon, Mr. Barrett. Welcome back to Crestline Uniform Rentals. I understand there was a problem with your last order — what can I help you with? M1: Yes, thanks. We received the staff uniforms for The Copper Kettle yesterday, but when the kitchen team tried them on, several of the jackets were the wrong size. A few are far too small for the people they were meant for. W1: Oh, I'm very sorry to hear that. That shouldn't have happened. Let me bring in Ingrid — she's the one who handles all of our stock and can sort this out for you right away. W2: Hello, Mr. Barrett, nice to meet you. I can see what went wrong, and we'll send out replacements in the correct sizes today. Before you leave, though, I'd recommend we go through the sizes on your order form together. That way we can be sure everything is recorded correctly and this won't come up again.

W1: Good morning. Do you have a reservation with us, or would you like to rent something today? M1: Good morning. I set everything up on your website last Tuesday — a complete ski package under the name Rourke — and I've come to collect it ahead of my weekend trip to Snowcrest Mountain. W1: Perfect, I've pulled it up using your confirmation number. You chose the standard package, but I'd suggest adding the damage waiver, since the trails at Snowcrest can be hard on the equipment. M1: That makes sense, so go ahead and add the waiver. I did think about a lesson, but a friend who skis often is coming with me, so I'll manage without one. W1: Sounds good. The skis and poles are already sized from your online details, but we always fit the boots in person, so the fitting area on your left is your next stop.

M1: Hi, this is Gordon Maloney. I'm calling because I'd like to book a deep clean for our office before the end of the week. We have an important inspection coming up. W1: Of course, Mr. Maloney. Thank you for calling Brightspan Cleaning Services. We have several openings this week. Would you also like to add on a carpet cleaning? It's a popular choice before an inspection. M1: The carpets were just replaced last month. W1: Oh, I see. Just the deep clean, then. What day and time works best for you? M1: Could you come Thursday evening, after six? The inspection is first thing Friday morning, so I'd really like everything to be spotless the night before.

W1: Hi there. My name's Gloria Hendricks. I noticed the recruitment notice pinned up over at the visitor center, and I've made up my mind — I'd like to donate some of my time here. What I'd enjoy most is helping to lead the guided nature walks for the public. M1: Wonderful, welcome! We're always glad to bring on new volunteers for the reserve. Could you tell me a bit about what you did before, and roughly when you'd be free to come in? W1: Certainly. I spent more than thirty years standing in front of a classroom before I retired a couple of years ago, so I'm quite comfortable managing groups of every age. Weekdays are tricky for me, but my weekends are wide open. M1: That works out well — the weekend slots are exactly when we run most of our public programs. There's one formality to sort out before you can begin, though. Let me bring in my colleague Trevor, since he oversees that side of things. M2: Hi there. Before we can add you to the schedule, you'll need to complete an orientation session. It runs through our safety and conservation guidelines, and it finishes with a guided loop along the main trails so you learn the routes. You can fill out your registration paperwork when you arrive that day. W1: That sounds really useful. So, when's the next one of those sessions being held?

M1: Good morning to you both. What can I do for you this morning? W1: Hi there. We'd like two tickets to Kelbridge, on the nine o'clock departure if there are still places. M1: Let me check the system for you. I'm afraid the nine o'clock filled up days ago, and there's nothing left on it at all. W2: Oh no. The thing is, we've got a meeting in Kelbridge, and we really can't arrive any later than noon. Is there anything else that would work? M1: There is. A faster service leaves from platform four at half past nine, and since it runs straight through without the smaller stops, it'll still put you in with plenty of time to spare. I'd point you toward that one. W1: Perfect. We'll take two on that one, then.

M1: All right, Yvonne. The carpet-cleaning machine you reserved last week is ready for you here at the counter. Before I hand any unit over, I always run it through a complete inspection, and I've just confirmed that all the attachments and the water tank are working the way they should. W1: Wonderful. A friend of mine told me this is the model I ought to ask for. M1: She's right. Most of our customers request this particular one, and it's not because it's the cheapest machine we rent out. It's built so that just one person can manage it alone, even loading it into a car or guiding it up a flight of stairs in a small apartment. W2: Sorry to break in on the two of you. M1: No problem, Bridget. I'm nearly finished here. What did you need? W2: I know you're busy with a customer, but there's a caller who's been holding on the line for a few minutes, and he says he'll only deal with you.

M1: Hi there. I'm looking to lease a retail space for a small bakery I'm opening. I noticed your agency had a unit listed on Calvert Street. Is it still available? M2: Yes, it is. That unit is about twelve hundred square feet, and the rent is two thousand dollars a month. It's on the ground floor of the building, right at the corner. W1: The real advantage of that corner is the number of people who walk past. There's a steady stream of pedestrians all day long, so the shops there get plenty of walk-in customers, and our current tenants are very happy about that. M1: That sounds perfect for a bakery. My only concern is parking. Is there anywhere close by for customers to leave their cars? M2: There's a public parking lot just around the block, so that shouldn't be an issue. I'd suggest we set up a viewing so you can see the space in person, and I'll pull a couple of our other listings for you to compare as well. Once everything's confirmed, I'll email you the lease paperwork. W1: That works. In the meantime, I'll reach out to the property owner this afternoon to check which times he has available.

W1: Hi, Dominic. I need to arrange travel for our annual marketing conference next month. I'll be attending on behalf of our whole department, and I was told this desk handles everything. M1: Yes, that's right. Here at the Redpoint travel desk we can book both your flight and your hotel, and there's a complimentary shuttle from the airport if you'd like it. Which dates will you be traveling? W1: I'll leave on the fourteenth and return three days later. The shuttle won't work for me, though. I'll need a rental car, since the venue is a good distance from the airport and I have meetings at several other sites. M1: No problem, I can add that in. But before I confirm anything, you'll need to submit an approval form signed by your manager. W1: Of course, I'll send that over later today. And once everything's booked, could you email me the complete itinerary so I have all the details together?

M1: Hi, I'm shopping for a gift. My closest friend just earned her degree, and I'd love to bring her something to mark the occasion. W1: How lovely! Does she happen to have a favorite type of chocolate? M1: She's fond of just about anything with nuts — almonds, hazelnuts, that sort of thing. W1: In that case, I'd point you to this one here. It's twenty-seven dollars, though our caramel selection is only fifteen if you'd prefer something lighter. M1: I don't need anything lighter — that first one sounds perfect. I'll take it. W1: Wonderful. And before you go, I'd be glad to dress it up with ribbon and paper. M1: Oh, that would be great. Thank you so much.

W1: Hi, I wonder if you could point me in the right direction. I'm looking for a sturdy pair of hiking boots — something for rough mountain trails. Do you carry those? M1: We do indeed. I should warn you, though — we reorganized the whole floor over the weekend, so several departments have shifted. The camping gear is up by the service counter now, and we moved all the clothing over to the right wall. Here's a store map so you can get your bearings. W1: That's good to know, thanks. Do you happen to stock the waterproof kind, and maybe in a wide fit? M1: We carry a full range of those. You'll find all the footwear over on the left, in the corner just opposite the service counter.

M1: Hi, good morning. I'm hoping to enroll in one of the cooking classes you're offering this week. W1: Wonderful — welcome to Larkspur Cooking School. Before I go over the availability with you, could you let me know whether you've done a fair amount of cooking, or whether you'd feel more comfortable starting in one of our beginner sessions? M1: Oh, I've been cooking at home for years, so I'd put myself somewhere around the intermediate level. And ideally I'd like a session in the afternoon, since I'm usually tied up with work in the mornings. W1: Of course. Let me pull up this week's schedule so you can see which sessions are still open and pick the one that fits both your level and the time you prefer. M1: Perfect. One more thing — will I need to bring along my own knives and ingredients, or is all of that something the school provides? W1: No need to bring a thing. We supply the ingredients, the aprons, and every piece of equipment you'll use. Just come ready to cook.

M: Good morning, and welcome back to Around Town, our weekly segment where I share a favorite new spot in the neighborhood. This week I stopped by Thistle and Vine, a restaurant that just opened over on Larkfield Avenue. I have to say, I was thoroughly impressed with just about everything. What really sets this place apart is that nearly all of the dishes on the menu are made with locally sourced ingredients from farms right here in our area. It's open for both lunch and dinner every day except Monday. And here's the best part for our listeners — if you visit their website and enter the code FRESH at checkout, you'll receive fifteen percent off your very first meal. So do give them a try.

W: Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you all for gathering here at Verano Creative Studio for this afternoon's team session. I'm delighted to introduce Diana Holt, who will be leading our hands-on workshop on digital illustration this afternoon. Over the past decade, Diana has created commissioned artwork for a range of well-known clients, and her illustrations have earned considerable recognition, appearing in several respected magazines both here and overseas. Diana and I once worked side by side at a small studio early in our careers, so it's a real pleasure to watch how far she has come. Before we begin, could everyone please add their name to the list that's making its way around the room? And now, let's welcome Diana up front to get us started.

M: After a long day at work, is figuring out what to cook the last thing you want to think about? With Freshfold Kitchen, a box of fresh ingredients and simple recipes arrives at your door every single week. Just pick your meals from our menu online, and we'll handle the rest. Every ingredient comes pre-measured and portioned for you, so a home-cooked dinner is ready in about thirty minutes. And don't just take our word for it—read what thousands of home cooks are saying about us online. Get fifty percent off your very first box at freshfold.com.

M: In local news, the Meadowlark Science Center has reported record-breaking attendance this season, though officials admit the surge has stretched the facility well beyond what it was originally built to handle. Center staff say the crowds are largely thanks to a brand-new exhibit on space exploration that opened just last month, which has proven far more popular than anyone had predicted. To cope, the center extended its daily hours and brought on extra weekend staff, yet long lines and packed galleries have still left some longtime members frustrated. The center's board is now weighing whether to limit daily admissions, a step that would disappoint first-time visitors but reassure regulars. So here's a tip for our listeners: if you're hoping to see the new exhibit, I'd book your tickets well ahead, because this weekend they sold out by early afternoon.

W: Hi, Mr. Coyle. This is Paula Grimes calling from Fairview Driving School. I just wanted to touch base with you ahead of your very first driving lesson, which we have scheduled for tomorrow morning at nine o'clock. To start things off, I'll swing by and collect you from the front entrance of your apartment building, so please try to be ready a few minutes early. Also, please don't forget to bring your learner's permit along, because we aren't allowed to begin the lesson without it. And one more thing: just for this week, we'll be meeting over at the Denby Street lot rather than our usual practice area, since the regular lot is being repaved at the moment. If anything comes up, feel free to call me back. Otherwise, I'll see you bright and early tomorrow.

W: Let's move on to a stock issue here at Thornbury's that we really need to sort out. Our cordless drills and power tools keep selling out much faster than we expected, and lately we can't keep them on the shelves at all. The trouble is that we rely on a single supplier, and recently they haven't managed to deliver enough to meet the demand. As a result, we're losing sales every week, and I've had several complaints from regular customers who left empty-handed. Some staff have suggested moving the display nearer the entrance, but that won't help if we've nothing to put out. So I'd like us to bring on a second supplier, so that our stock stays steady going forward. Having another source would also cushion us against any future delays if one vendor falls behind. Now, who would like to look into this and track down a dependable new vendor for us?

W: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us tonight. As the director of Fenwick Creative Group, I'm delighted to welcome you to our yearly celebration of the very best work produced at our agency. Each year, we recognize the team whose efforts made the greatest impact on our clients over the past twelve months. This year's honor goes to our brand team, whose campaign reached audiences right across the country and set a new standard for everyone here. To help us celebrate, we've invited a very special guest, Ronald Vasquez, a respected industry figure who founded the well-known firm Vasquez Media more than two decades ago. Now, please join me in welcoming Mr. Vasquez to the stage to hand this year's trophy to our winning brand team.

W: You're listening to WBRT, Hartwell's community radio station. In business news this morning, a local favorite is being celebrated. Fernway Garden Supply, the family-run store on Bramford Road, has just been named Employer of the Year by the regional business association. The award recognizes the company's outstanding staff training and its brand-new apprenticeship program. Managing director Angela Corbett says she is deeply passionate about developing young employees and giving them a real start in their careers. Now, the store admits it struggled for years to interest school graduates in the trade, so this spring's intake was never a sure thing. Still, she plans to double the size of the apprenticeship program over the next two years, and given how quickly the latest openings were snapped up, that target may prove easier to reach than anyone expected.

W: Tired of driving around in a dusty, streaky car? Then it's time to visit Silverline Auto Wash, your neighborhood full-service car wash. We offer a full range of cleaning packages, from a quick basic wash all the way up to a complete interior and exterior detailing. And here's something we're really proud of — we use a water-recycling system that saves thousands of liters of water every single day. Booking a visit is easy: just download our mobile app and reserve a time that works for you. Right now, we also have a special welcome offer for all first-time customers. Choose any package above our entry-level wash, and you'll drive away with a complimentary air freshener!

W: Hi, Gemma. I'm calling about the staff training seminar our department is organizing for next month. I just finished reviewing the registration list, and I was really pleased to see how many people from our regional offices have already signed up. We still need to decide which vendor to hire for the audio-visual equipment, so I've put together a comparison of four rental companies and the best feature that each one offers, and I've sent it over to you. One of them delivers and sets everything up for free, which is a very attractive offer given our limited budget. But another company sends a technician to stay on-site throughout the entire event to handle any equipment problems that come up. I think that kind of support would really put everyone at ease, so that's the one I recommend.
